andalusia.answer: Andalusia taxes a home bought by a large family at 3.5% instead of the general 7%, when the value is up to €250,000.
andalusia.note: Main-home condition not stated in the report for this case.

sources.title: Ley 5/2021, Andalusia, art. 43 (BOE)

aragon.conditions: Art. 121-5: purchase of the family's main home; previous home sold between two years before and four years after (waived for a first main home); usable area at least 10% larger; income (general base plus part of the savings base, less personal and descendant minimums) at most €35,000 plus €6,000 per child above the legal minimum.
aragon.answer: Aragon gives large families a 50% bonus on the transfer tax if income is up to €35,000 plus €6,000 per extra child; the general rate runs from 8% to 10%.
aragon.note: Settled on art. 121-5 (BOE consolidated text, read 15 Oct. 2026); the article sets no price cap.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2005, Aragon, art. 121-5 (BOE)

asturias.conditions: Main home (art. 32 bis); same article covers single-parent families, young buyers and rural areas.
asturias.answer: Asturias taxes a large family's main home at 4% up to €150,000 and 6% above, instead of the general 8% to 10%.
asturias.note: Price cap null: €150,000 is a rate threshold.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 2/2014, Asturias, art. 32 bis (BOE)

balearic-islands.conditions: Art. 10.d also covers under-36 first-home buyers, disability and single-parent families.
balearic-islands.answer: The Balearic Islands tax a large family's purchase at 2%, against a general rate of 8% to 13%.
balearic-islands.note: The conditions of article 10.d for large families are not detailed in the report; no price cap read.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2014, Balearic Islands, arts. 10, 14 quater (BOE)

basque-country.conditions: Main home (vivienda habitual); no other home held above 25% in the municipality; or a home of 120 m2 built or less.
basque-country.answer: In the three Basque territories, a large family buying a main home pays 2.5% transfer tax instead of the 4% housing rate, if it owns no other home above 25% in the municipality.
basque-country.note: In Gipuzkoa the area test is 120 m2 built or 96 m2 usable; Álava and Bizkaia give 2.5% for 120 m2 or large family. Price cap not read.

sources.title: Basque Government, list of ITP and AJD regulations
Norma Foral 11/2003, Álava, updated text (Diputación Foral de Álava)

canary-islands.conditions: Income up to €46,455 (arts. 32, 33, 33 bis; also disability, single-parent families); no other home (guide).
canary-islands.answer: The Canary Islands tax a large family's home at 1% (arts. 32, 33, 33 bis) with an income cap of €46,455, against a general rate of 6.5%.
canary-islands.note: The guide adds an income supplement per child and the no-other-home test; the report gives only the €46,455 figure. Price cap not read for the 1% rate.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2009, Canary Islands, arts. 31, 35 (BOE)

cantabria.answer: Cantabria taxes a large family's purchase at 4% on the first €300,000 of value, against a general rate of 9%.
cantabria.note: Reduced rates are limited to the first €300,000 (art. 9.7).

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 62/2008, Cantabria, art. 9 (BOE)

castile-and-leon.conditions: Main home; income cap €31,500, or €37,800 for large families plus €6,000 per member (art. 28).
castile-and-leon.answer: Castile and León taxes a large family's main home at 4% instead of 8% and 10%, with an income cap of €37,800 plus €6,000 per member.
castile-and-leon.note: Settled on arts. 25.3.a and 28.2 (BOE consolidated text last updated 14/05/2024, read 15 Oct. 2026): if the buyer already owns a home, it must be sold within one year of buying the new one; no price cap in these articles.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2013, Castile and León, arts. 25, 28 (BOE)

castilla-la-mancha.conditions: Large or single-parent family, or disability of 65% or more (Ley 1/2026).
castilla-la-mancha.answer: Castilla-La Mancha taxes a first main home bought by a large-family member, a single-parent family member or a person with disability of 65% or more at 5% instead of the general 9%, when the value is up to €240,000 and the purchase is financed more than 50% by a mortgage.
castilla-la-mancha.note: Settled on Ley 1/2026, art. 18 amending art. 19.6 of Ley 8/2013 (DOCM 30 March 2026, in force 31 March 2026; not yet in the BOE consolidated text). Value must also be at least the mortgage valuation where no reference value exists, and the declared value at least the reference value.

sources.title: Ley 1/2026, Castilla-La Mancha, art. 18 (DOCM 30/03/2026, BOE copy)

catalonia.conditions: Art. 641-2: main home; sum of the general and savings bases less personal and family minimums of the family members in the last income tax return at most €36,000, plus €14,000 per child above the legal minimum for large-family status.
catalonia.answer: Catalonia taxes a large family's main home at 5% instead of 10% to 13%, if family income is at most €36,000 plus €14,000 per child above the legal minimum.
catalonia.note: Settled on art. 641-2 (BOE consolidated text, read 15 Oct. 2026); the article sets no price cap.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2024, Catalonia, art. 641-2 (BOE)

ceuta.answer: Ceuta has no own large-family rate in the report: the national 6% rate with a 50% bonus gives an effective 3% for every buyer.
ceuta.note: The report gives no own regional rates.

sources.title: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1993, consolidated ITPAJD text (BOE)
AEAT, Base imponible y tipos Ceuta y Melilla

community-of-madrid.conditions: Art. 29: buyer holds the large-family title and the property is the family's main home; if the previous main home belonged to a holder, it must be sold within two years before or after (waived when the new property is joined to the old home).
community-of-madrid.answer: The Community of Madrid taxes large families at 4% instead of the general 6%.
community-of-madrid.note: Settled on art. 29 (BOE consolidated text, read 15 Oct. 2026); the article sets no price cap or income cap.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, Community of Madrid, arts. 30 bis, 38 bis (BOE)

extremadura.conditions: Main home; income up to €30,000 (€55,000 joint) (art. 41).

andalusia.answer: Andalusia applies a 3.5% transfer tax (ITP) rate to buyers under 35 who buy a main home worth up to €150,000, against the general rate of 7%.
andalusia.note: No income cap read in the report.

sources.title: Ley 5/2021, Andalusia, art. 43 (BOE)

aragon.conditions: Bonus of 12.5% of the tax (art. 121-4), also for disability of 65% or more and victims of gender violence.
aragon.answer: Aragon gives buyers under 35 a 12.5% bonus on the transfer tax when the home is worth up to €100,000; the general rate runs from 8% to 10% by value.
aragon.note: Settled on art. 121-4 (BOE consolidated text, read 15 Oct. 2026): 12.5% bonus on the full tax for buyers under 35, main home, real value of the property not above €100,000; no income cap in the article.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2005, Aragon, art. 121-4 (BOE)

asturias.conditions: Main home, resale; live there within 6 months and for 3 years (guide). Same article also covers rural areas, large and single-parent families.
asturias.answer: Asturias taxes a main home bought by a buyer up to 35 at 4% up to €150,000 and 6% above, instead of the general 8% to 10% (art. 32 bis, in force 1 January 2026).
asturias.note: Price cap null: €150,000 is a rate threshold, not a ceiling. The occupancy deadlines come from the guide only.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 2/2014, Asturias, art. 32 bis (BOE)

balearic-islands.conditions: 2% route: first home, under 36. Bonus route: under 30 or disability of 33% or more, 3 years' residence, mortgage of 60% or more.
balearic-islands.answer: The Balearic Islands charge 2% transfer tax to buyers under 36 buying a first home, and give a 100% bonus to buyers under 30 who meet residence, income (€52,800, or €84,480 joint), value (€270,151.20) and mortgage (60% or more) tests; the general rate runs from 8% to 13%.
balearic-islands.note: Settled on the BOE consolidated text (read 15 Oct. 2026): art. 10.d applies the 2% rate only if all conditions of art. 10.c are met, including the €270,151.20 maximum value, main home, at least 50% acquired and no other home held at 50% or more; the 2% route for a first home needs a buyer under 36 (art. 10.d.1). Art. 14 quater (100% bonus, under 30 or disability of 33% or more) has its own €270,151.20 cap, three years' residence, a first home, income cap and a mortgage of 60% or more of the valuation.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2014, Balearic Islands, arts. 10, 14 quater (BOE)

basque-country.answer: The three Basque territories (Álava, Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa) have no young-buyer rate in their ITP norma foral texts read on 15 Oct. 2026: a home pays 4% whatever the buyer's age, and 2.5% under the area or large-family tests.
basque-country.note: Settled on the texts of Norma Foral 11/2003 (Álava), 1/2011 (Bizkaia) and 18/1987 (Gipuzkoa), searched for any young-buyer (jóvenes) rate: none found.

sources.title: Norma Foral 11/2003, Álava, updated text (Diputación Foral de Álava)
Norma Foral 1/2011, Bizkaia, consolidated text (Diputación Foral de Bizkaia)
Norma Foral 18/1987, Gipuzkoa, information copy (Diputación Foral de Gipuzkoa)

canary-islands.conditions: First main home, no property owned (5% rate: main home, base up to €200,000, no other home).
canary-islands.answer: The Canary Islands give buyers aged 40 or under a 20% bonus on the transfer tax computed at the 5% main-home rate, for a first main home with value up to €200,000 and income up to €46,455 plus €6,825 per dependant; the general rate is 6.5%.
canary-islands.note: The report lists art. 35 as a 20% bonus (40 or under) but its text is cut off; the income cap and the dependant supplement come from the guide only, and the report ties €46,455 to other articles.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2009, Canary Islands, arts. 31, 35 (BOE)

cantabria.conditions: Main home; the excess above €300,000 pays 9%.
cantabria.answer: Cantabria taxes a main home bought by a buyer under 40 at 4% on the first €300,000 of value, with the 9% general rate on any excess.
cantabria.note: Settled on art. 9.3.c (BOE consolidated text, read 15 Oct. 2026): buyer under 40 at the date of purchase, main home; no income cap in that article. The reduced rate is limited to the first €300,000 (art. 9.7).

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 62/2008, Cantabria, art. 9 (BOE)

castile-and-leon.age_limit: under 36 (all buyers); 0.01% for under 36 in rural communes
castile-and-leon.answer: Castile and León taxes a main home bought by a buyer under 36 at 4% (0.01% in rural communes), with an income cap of €31,500, against the general 8% and 10%.
castile-and-leon.note: Settled on arts. 25.3 and 28.2 (BOE consolidated text last updated 14/05/2024, read 15 Oct. 2026): all buyers under 36 at the date of accrual, main home, first home of each buyer; total taxable bases less personal and family minimum at most €31,500; no price cap in these articles. The rural 0.01% rate applies to housing in a commune listed in art. 7.1.c.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2013, Castile and León, arts. 25, 28 (BOE)

castilla-la-mancha.conditions: First main home; mortgage above 50% of the price (guide). AJD 0.25% for under-36s.
castilla-la-mancha.answer: Castilla-La Mancha charges 3% transfer tax, instead of 9%, to buyers under 36 of a first main home worth up to €240,000, and 0.25% stamp duty (AJD) on a new home.
castilla-la-mancha.note: Settled on the text of Ley 1/2026, art. 18 (DOCM 30 March 2026, in force 31 March 2026; not yet in the BOE consolidated text): the €240,000 cap applies to each of the 6% (art. 19.2), 5% (19.6), 3% under-36 (19.9) rates and to the AJD rates (art. 21.2: 0.75%, 0.50%, 0.25%). Also required: mortgage above 50% of the value, value at least the mortgage valuation where no reference value exists, and declared value at least the reference value. Lower rates apply in depopulation-risk municipalities (5%, 4%, 3%).

sources.title: Ley 1/2026, Castilla-La Mancha, art. 18 (DOCM 30/03/2026, BOE copy)

catalonia.conditions: Main home; stamp duty (AJD) 100% bonus for the same group (art. 642-6).
catalonia.answer: Catalonia taxes buyers aged 35 or under at 5% (income up to €36,000) instead of 10% to 13%, and gives them a 100% bonus on stamp duty on a new home.
catalonia.note: Settled on art. 641-5 (BOE consolidated text, read 15 Oct. 2026; rate in force since 27/06/2025): the 5% rate applies to a main home bought by a buyer aged 35 or under at the date of tax accrual, if the sum of the general and savings bases less the personal and family minimum in the last income tax return does not exceed €36,000; the article sets no price cap.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2024, Catalonia, arts. 641-5, 642-6 (BOE)

ceuta.answer: Ceuta has no own transfer tax rates: the national 6% rate applies with a 50% bonus, which gives an effective 3% for every buyer, and no young-buyer rate appears in the report.
ceuta.note: The report gives no own regional rates; the effective 3% is not a young-buyer rate.

sources.title: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1993, consolidated ITPAJD text (BOE)
AEAT, Base imponible y tipos Ceuta y Melilla

community-of-madrid.conditions: Only in a municipality with fewer than 2,500 inhabitants; main home. Everyone else gets a 10% bonus on the tax for a main home up to €250,000.
community-of-madrid.answer: The Community of Madrid gives a 100% bonus on the transfer tax to buyers under 35 of a main home worth up to €250,000, but only in a municipality under 2,500 inhabitants; the general rate is 6%.
community-of-madrid.note: Settled on the BOE consolidated text (read 15 Oct. 2026): art. 30 bis (ITP, last update in force 29/11/2024) gives a 10% bonus on the tax to any main-home buyer, and 100% to buyers under 35 in a municipality under 2,500 inhabitants (INE figure at 1 January of the year before); art. 38 bis gives the same on the AJD graduated quota of first copies. Both require a value up to €250,000 (garages and annexes included). There is no reduced rate by age; the only age-based benefit is that 100% bonus.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, Community of Madrid, arts. 30 bis, 38 bis (BOE)

extremadura.conditions: Main home (art. 41, with the same conditions as art. 40).
extremadura.answer: Extremadura taxes a main home bought by a buyer under 36 at 4% (general 8% to 11%) when the value is up to €200,000 and income up to €30,000, or €55,000 joint.
extremadura.note: Article 40 bis, a young-buyer rate, was repealed from 5 August 2026 by Ley 2/2026.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2018, Extremadura, arts. 40, 41 (BOE)

galicia.price_cap: €240,000 plus €30,000 per extra household member (price and assets)
galicia.answer: Galicia taxes a main home bought by a buyer under 36 at 3% instead of the general 8%.
galicia.note: Settled on the BOE consolidated text (read 15 Oct. 2026): art. 14.Dos (7% main-home rate) and art. 14.Cinco (3% rate, under 36 at the date of tax accrual) each set the same cap on the purchase price and on the buyers' (and household's) assets: €240,000 plus €30,000 per household member beyond the first. The deed must state the buyer's birth date and the main-home purpose. The cap therefore applies to the 3% rate as well.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2011, Galicia, art. 14 (BOE)

la-rioja.answer: La Rioja taxes a first main home bought by a buyer under 40 at 4%, or 3% in the municipalities of the law's annex I, against the general 7%.
la-rioja.note: Settled on art. 45.3 (BOE consolidated text, read 15 Oct. 2026): the 4% rate (3% in annex I municipalities) applies to a first main home bought by a buyer under 40 at the date of purchase; the article sets no price cap and no income cap.

sources.title: Ley 10/2017, La Rioja, art. 45 (BOE)

melilla.answer: Melilla has no own transfer tax rates: the national 6% rate applies with a 50% bonus, which gives an effective 3% for every buyer, and no young-buyer rate appears in the report.
melilla.note: The report gives no own regional rates; the effective 3% is not a young-buyer rate.

sources.title: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1993, consolidated ITPAJD text (BOE)
AEAT, Base imponible y tipos Ceuta y Melilla

murcia.income_cap: general base less personal minimum under €40,000 (savings base at most €1,800)
murcia.answer: The Region of Murcia taxes a main home bought by a buyer aged 40 or under at 3% instead of 7.75%, if the general taxable base less the personal minimum is under €40,000.
murcia.note: Settled on art. 6.6 (BOE consolidated text, read 15 Oct. 2026): age 40 or under, main home, general taxable base less personal and family minimum under €40,000 and savings base at most €1,800; the article sets no price cap.

sources.title: Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, Region of Murcia, art. 6 (BOE)

navarre.answer: Navarre has no young-buyer rate in article 8 of its ITP text (read 15 Oct. 2026): the general rate is 6%, with 5% for families with two children or more and 4% in municipalities at risk of depopulation.
navarre.note: Settled on article 8 of Decreto Foral Legislativo 129/1999 (consolidated text updated 20/04/2026), read for any rate tied to the buyer's age: none found.

sources.title: Decreto Foral Legislativo 129/1999, Navarre, consolidated ITPAJD text (BOE)

valencian-community.answer: The Valencian Community taxes a first main home bought by a buyer under 35 at 6% up to €180,000 and 8% above, against a general 9%.
valencian-community.note: The report gives the 8% and 6% rates with the €180,000 threshold but not which side each applies to; the income figures come from the guide only.

sources.title: Ley 13/1997, Valencian Community, arts. 4, 13 (BOE)

guides.title: Inheritance tax in Spain for non-residents

guides.title: Land registry fees in Spain: scale, cap and reductions
guides.description: Spain's land registry fee under RD 1427/1989: the scale, the cap, the two 5% reductions, the presentation entry, and why registering protects the buyer.

guides.title: Letting your property in Spain: landlord obligations
guides.description: What a landlord in Spain must do: written contract terms, deposit, energy label, habitability papers, repairs, advertising rules and where the tax guides start.

guides.title: Main home reinvestment exemption in Spain
guides.description: A Spanish resident who reinvests a main home sale in a new one within two years can exclude the gain (art. 38 Ley 35/2006). Conditions and who is left out.

guides.title: Military zones: when non-EU buyers need an authorisation
guides.description: Ley 8/1975 and Royal Decree 689/1978: which areas need a Ministry of Defence authorisation for non-EU buyers, the urban exemption and the application steps.

guides.title: Modelo 210: the non-resident tax return explained
guides.description: What a non-resident declares on modelo 210: imputed income, rent, sale gains. Deadlines under Orden HAC/623/2026, grouping, refunds and how to file.

guides.title: Modelo 720: declaring foreign property from Spain
guides.description: Modelo 720 is Spain's return for assets abroad. Who files, the €50,000 property threshold, 1 January to 31 March, and the changes brought by Ley 5/2022.

guides.title: Who pays the mortgage costs in Spain: lender or borrower
guides.description: How Ley 5/2019 splits notary, registry, gestoría, valuation and copy costs on a Spanish mortgage, and who is the taxpayer for the stamp duty (AJD) on the deed.

guides.title: Getting a Spanish mortgage as a non-resident
guides.description: Ley 5/2019 protects any individual borrowing for a home in Spain, resident or not. What the law sets, what lenders decide (no legal LTV cap) and the paperwork.

guides.title: How a mortgage works in Spain: Ley 5/2019 explained
guides.description: The national rules for a Spanish home loan: the FEIN and FiAE offer documents, the 10-day wait, free notary advice, the ban on tied sales and complaints.

guides.title: NIE number for property buyers in Spain
guides.description: What the NIE is, why a foreign buyer needs it for the deed and taxes, the €9.84 fee in Spain, the five-day term and why silence means refusal.

guides.title: Non-resident property tax in Spain: imputed income
guides.description: Owning a Spanish home you do not let: annual non-resident tax on 2% or 1.1% of the cadastral value, at 24% or 19%, with a worked example and the 2027 change.

guides.title: Nota simple: the Spanish land registry extract explained
guides.description: What a nota simple shows (owner, charges), how to order it from the Colegio de Registradores, the €9.02 fee as read, and why it is not a certificate.

guides.title: Notary fees in Spain: the official scale for a sale
guides.description: Spanish notary fees under RD 1426/1989: the scale on the price, the 5% rebate, copies and pages, the optional 10% discount, who pays and what the notary checks.

guides.title: Over-65 exemption on selling a main home in Spain
guides.description: Over 65 and selling your main home in Spain: the gain is exempt from income tax (art. 33.4.b Ley 35/2006). Conditions, the annuity route and non-residents.

guides.title: Plusvalía municipal: the Spanish land value tax
guides.description: How Spain's plusvalía municipal is worked out since RDL 26/2021: objective or real-gain method, the coefficients in force, the 30% cap, who pays and when.

guides.title: ITP: transfer tax on a resale home in Spain, by region
guides.description: ITP is paid by the buyer of a resale home in Spain and the rate is set by each region, from 6% to 13%. Table of the 19 general rates, base and how to read it.

guides.title: Property valuation (tasación) for a Spanish mortgage
guides.description: Who may value a home for a Spanish mortgage: valuers approved by the Banco de España, Orden ECO/805/2003, who pays, bringing your own report, validity.

guides.title: Proposed tax on non-EU buyers in Spain: status, not law
guides.description: No Spanish law taxes property purchases by non-EU buyers on 15 October 2026. What the BOE and the dissolution of the Cortes mean for any pending proposal.

guides.title: Reduced transfer tax for young buyers in Spain, by region
guides.description: Region-by-region reduced ITP and AJD for young buyers in Spain: age limits, price caps and income caps for 15 regions. Conditions are cumulative.

guides.title: Catastro reference value: tax base on a Spanish purchase
guides.description: In Spain the Catastro's valor de referencia is the tax base for ITP and AJD unless the price is higher. How it is set, published and contested.

guides.title: Rent aid for young people in Spain (Plan 2026-2030)
guides.description: Youth rent aid in Spain's housing plan 2026-2030: under 35, income and rent caps, up to €300 a month for 2 years. Basque Country and Navarre are out.

guides.title: Rent increases in Spain: the IRAV index and the 2% rule
guides.description: How a Spanish residential rent may be updated: no clause means no increase, the IRAV cap (2.54% in September 2026) and the 2% temporary rule to end-2027.

guides.title: Letting agency fees in Spain: why the landlord pays
guides.description: Article 20.2 of Spain's tenancy law bars passing agency and contract-signing costs to the tenant, directly or indirectly. What it covers and what you still pay.

guides.title: Rental deposit (fianza) in Spain: amount, filing, return
guides.description: The Spanish rental deposit is one month's rent by law, plus a capped extra guarantee. Regional bodies hold it: six regions' rules, and getting it back.

guides.title: Rental income tax for residents of Spain (IRPF)
guides.description: How a Spanish tax resident is taxed on home rental income (IRPF): net income, deductible costs and the article 23.2 reductions, 15% to 100%.

guides.title: Renting a home in Spain: tenant rights and contract terms
guides.description: How long a Spanish residential lease lasts (5 or 7 years), how extensions work after the October 2026 decree-laws, notice periods and your right to stay.

guides.title: Renting out a Spanish home as a non-resident: tax
guides.description: Rent from a Spanish home is taxed at 24% on gross income outside the EU and EEA, and at 19% after expenses for EU and EEA residents. Dates and examples.

guides.title: Selling a home in Spain: what the seller pays
guides.description: What a seller pays in Spain: plusvalía municipal, income tax on the gain, the buyer's 3% withholding, energy certificate, mortgage cancellation and deed costs.

guides.title: Selling Spanish property as a non-resident: 3% withholding
guides.description: A non-resident seller in Spain: the buyer withholds 3% (modelo 211), the gain is taxed at 19% (modelo 210). Reinvestment exemption and who pays plusvalía.

guides.title: Spain-Canada tax treaty and Spanish property
guides.description: What the 1976 Canada-Spain tax convention says about rent from and gains on Spanish real estate, and how double tax is eliminated, in plain words.

guides.title: The Spain–UK tax treaty and your Spanish property
guides.description: What the 2013 UK–Spain double taxation convention says about rent, sale gains and wealth on Spanish property: articles 4, 6, 13, 21 and 22, with limits.

guides.title: Will and succession law for a Spanish property: EU 650/2012
guides.description: Which law governs the estate of an owner of a Spanish home: habitual residence, choice of national law (art. 22), the European Certificate and wills.

guides.title: Stamp duty (AJD) on a Spanish mortgage: the lender pays
guides.description: Since November 2018 the lender, not the borrower, is the taxpayer of AJD on a mortgage deed in Spain. What the borrower still pays and regional rates.

guides.title: Stressed housing market areas (zonas tensionadas) in Spain
guides.description: What a declared stressed rental zone changes in Spain: rent caps on new leases, longer extensions, tax effects, and regions with zones in the BOE.

guides.title: Tax representative for non-resident owners in Spain
guides.description: When a non-resident owner in Spain must appoint a tax representative under article 10 of the IRNR law, when not, the two-month notice and the €2,000 fixed fine.

guides.title: Tax residency in Spain: the 183-day rule explained
guides.description: When you become tax resident in Spain under article 9 of the IRPF law, how treaty tie-breakers work, and what changes: worldwide income, modelo 720, wealth tax.

guides.title: Total buying costs in Spain: every line, who pays
guides.description: Every cost of buying a home in Spain: ITP or VAT plus stamp duty, notary, registry, valuation, gestoría. Who pays by default, with a €300,000 worked example.

guides.title: Tourist rental registration in Spain after the 2026 rulings
guides.description: Spain's single rental register was struck down in part by the Supreme Court in May-June 2026. What remains: regional tourist registers and local licences.

guides.title: Tourist rentals and the community of owners in Spain
guides.description: Since 3 April 2025 a Spanish owner needs the community's express approval, by a 3/5 vote, for a tourist let in a flat. Majorities, existing lets, remedies.

guides.title: Property transfer tax in Andalusia: 7% ITP and AJD
guides.description: Andalusia charges a flat 7% ITP on resale homes and 1.2% AJD on new ones. Reduced rates, their price caps, a worked example and notes for non-resident buyers.

guides.title: Balearic Islands transfer tax: 8% to 13% and AJD 2%
guides.description: Balearic resale homes pay ITP on an average-rate scale from 8% to 13%; AJD is 1.5%, or 2% from €1 million. The 4% and 2% rates, art. 14 quater, examples.

guides.title: Basque Country and Navarre: 4% home transfer tax
guides.description: Álava, Bizkaia and Gipuzkoa tax a home purchase at 4% (2.5% in some cases); Navarre at 6%. AJD is 0.5%, the base is real value, and VAT is as elsewhere.

guides.title: Canary Islands purchase taxes: ITP 6.5%, IGIC 7%
guides.description: In the Canary Islands a resale home pays 6.5% ITP (5% for a main residence up to €200,000) and a new home pays IGIC, not VAT. Rates, conditions and examples.

guides.title: Buying in Catalonia: ITP from 10% to 13%, and 20%
guides.description: Catalonia taxes resale homes at 10% up to €600,000, rising to 13%, and 20% for large holders. AJD, reduced rates for under-35s, examples and non-resident notes.

guides.title: Madrid property tax: 6% ITP and the AJD scale
guides.description: Madrid charges 6% ITP on resale homes and a 0.4% to 0.75% AJD scale on new ones. The 10% reduction up to €250,000 and the smoothing rule explained.

guides.title: Murcia property transfer tax: 7.75% ITP since July 2025
guides.description: Murcia charges a flat 7.75% ITP on resale property since 25 July 2025 and 1.5% AJD on new homes. The 3% rate for under-40s, large families and disability.

guides.title: Valencian Community: 9% ITP since June 2026, 11% over €1m
guides.description: Resale homes in the Valencian Community pay 9% ITP from 1 June 2026, and 11% on the whole price above €1 million. AJD, young-buyer rates and a worked example.

guides.title: UK buyers in Spain after Brexit: what changed
guides.description: How Brexit changed Spanish rules for UK owners: 24% tax on gross rent, military-zone permits, the 90/180-day limit, and what the Withdrawal Agreement keeps.

guides.title: VAT and stamp duty on a new home in Spain
guides.description: A new home in Spain carries 10% VAT (4% for some protected housing) plus regional stamp duty (AJD) on the deed. Rates by region and the 2026 change.

guides.title: Wealth tax for non-residents who own Spanish property
guides.description: How Spain's wealth tax and the €3m solidarity tax apply to non-resident owners: the €700,000 allowance, regional rules and the compulsory representative.

professions.title: Architects and technical architects in Spain
professions.description: Architects (arquitectos) and technical architects (aparejadores) in Spain: college membership, roles under the LOE, when to use one and how to check.

professions.title: Mortgage lenders in Spain: how to check one
professions.description: Banks, other mortgage lenders and credit intermediaries in Spain must be registered with the Banco de España or their region. The rules and how to check.

professions.title: Property lawyers in Spain: what they do, how to check
professions.description: What an abogado does in a Spanish property purchase, compulsory bar membership, how to check the CGAE census, the notary's separate role. Informational page.

professions.title: Property valuers in Spain: approved appraisal firms
professions.description: A valuation for a Spanish mortgage must come from an approved appraisal firm registered with the Banco de España. What the rules say and how to check one.

professions.title: Real estate agents in Spain: registers and fees
professions.description: Estate agency is free nationally in Spain, but Catalonia and Valencia require a register entry. What the API title means, how to check, and who pays in a rental.
